{
  "measurements": [
    {
      "statistic": "failure rate",
      "value": 80.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "potential therapeutics that fail when tested in people after animal studies suggest they will be safe and effective",
      "compared": "animal studies vs human testing",
      "species": ["mouse", "human"],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "potential therapeutics",
      "verbatim": "Even after animal studies suggest that a treatment will be safe and effective, more than 80% of potential therapeutics fail when tested in people."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "failure rate",
      "value": 100.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "experimental treatments for ALS that had been shown to ameliorate disease in an animal model but failed in the clinic",
      "compared": "animal models of ALS vs human clinical trials",
      "species": ["mouse", "human"],
      "n": 12,
      "n_counts": "experimental treatments for ALS",
      "verbatim": "Over the past decade, about a dozen experimental treatments have made their way into human trials for ALS. All had been shown to ameliorate disease in an established animal model. All but one failed in the clinic"
    },
    {
      "statistic": "benefit rate",
      "value": 0.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "experimental treatments for ALS that had been shown to ameliorate disease in an animal model and were found to be beneficial in the clinic",
      "compared": "animal models of ALS vs human clinical trials",
      "species": ["mouse", "human"],
      "n": 11,
      "n_counts": "experimental treatments for ALS",
      "verbatim": "All but one failed in the clinic, and the survival benefits of that one are marginal."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "benefit rate",
      "value": 0.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "potential drugs tested in an ALS mouse model that were found to be beneficial in ALS TDI's experiments, despite being reported to slow disease",
      "compared": "reported animal study results vs ALS TDI's animal study results",
      "species": ["mouse"],
      "n": 100,
      "n_counts": "potential drugs",
      "verbatim": "Many of these drugs had been reported to slow down disease in that same mouse model; none was found to be beneficial in our experiments (see ‘Due diligence, overdue’)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "failure rate",
      "value": 100.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "compounds that failed in clinical trials after being tested in an ALS mouse model by ALS TDI",
      "compared": "compounds tested in ALS mouse model vs compounds in human clinical trials",
      "species": ["mouse", "human"],
      "n": 8,
      "n_counts": "compounds",
      "verbatim": "Eight of these compounds ultimately failed in clinical trials, which together involved thousands of people."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "variation in lifespan",
      "value": 10.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "variation in the average lifespan of SOD1 mice",
      "compared": "lifespan of SOD1 mice",
      "species": ["mouse"],
      "n": 5500,
      "n_counts": "mice",
      "verbatim": "Almost 90% of the mice had an average lifespan of 134 days, give or take 10 days."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "survival benefit",
      "value": 30.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "survival boost in SOD1 mice treated with lithium",
      "compared": "SOD1 mice treated with lithium vs untreated SOD1 mice",
      "species": ["mouse"],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "SOD1 mice",
      "verbatim": "This is exemplified by a study showing that lithium can boost survival of SOD1 mice by 30 days, an astoundingly long time8."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "survival benefit",
      "value": 30.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "days of survival extension in people with ALS treated with lithium",
      "compared": "people with ALS treated with lithium vs untreated people with ALS",
      "species": ["human"],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "people with ALS",
      "verbatim": "A small clinical trial showed that it also extended life in people with ALS8."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "cost to characterize a single drug",
      "value": 330000.0,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "cost to determine if a single drug has reasonable potential to treat disease in humans",
      "compared": "drug characterization vs clinical development",
      "species": ["human"],
      "n": 1,
      "n_counts": "drug",
      "verbatim": "an investment of $330,000 is necessary just to determine whether a single drug has reasonable potential to treat disease in humans."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "cost to characterize toxicity",
      "value": 30000.0,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "cost to characterize the toxicity of a molecule and assess its potential effectiveness",
      "compared": "molecule toxicity characterization",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "molecule",
      "verbatim": "We estimate that it takes about $30,000 and 6–9 months to characterize the toxicity of a molecule and assess whether enough reaches the relevant tissue and has a sufficient half life at the target to be potentially effective."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "cost to test survival benefit",
      "value": 100000.0,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "cost to test whether a drug can extend an animal's survival",
      "compared": "drug survival benefit testing in animals",
      "species": ["animal"],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "drug",
      "verbatim": "If those results are promising, then experiments to test whether a drug can extend an animal’s survival are warranted — this will cost about $100,000 per dose and take around 12 months."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "number of doses to test",
      "value": 3.0,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "number of doses of a molecule that should be tested to establish real drug responses",
      "compared": "molecule dosing levels",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "molecule",
      "verbatim": "At least three doses of the molecule should be tested; this will help to establish that any drug responses are real and suggest what a reasonable dosing level might be."
    }
  ],
  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study discusses the challenges and limitations of preclinical animal research in predicting human therapeutic outcomes, particularly in the context of ALS.",
  "what_it_found": "A high percentage of potential therapeutics fail in human trials after showing promise in animal studies, often due to inadequately designed preclinical experiments and a lack of rigorous characterization of animal models.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "Even after animal studies suggest that a treatment will be safe and effective, more than 80% of potential therapeutics fail when tested in people.",
      "topic": "High failure rate"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Animal models of disease are frequently condemned as poor predictors of whether an experimental drug can become an effective treatment.",
      "topic": "Poor predictors"
    },
    {
      "quote": "All had been shown to ameliorate disease in an established animal model. All but one failed in the clinic",
      "topic": "ALS trial failures"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Many of these drugs had been reported to slow down disease in that same mouse model; none was found to be beneficial in our experiments",
      "topic": "TDI experiment results"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Almost 90% of the mice had an average lifespan of 134 days, give or take 10 days.",
      "topic": "Mouse lifespan variation"
    },
    {
      "quote": "an investment of $330,000 is necessary just to determine whether a single drug has reasonable potential to treat disease in humans.",
      "topic": "Characterization cost"
    }
  ]
